title: Former Health Official Anthony Fauci Refuses to Answer Questions at Senate Hearing
subtitle: Dr. Fauci uses his constitutional right to remain silent during a tense meeting about the origins of Covid-19.

summary.en: Former top US health official Anthony Fauci recently appeared before a US Senate committee. During the hearing, he chose to use his Fifth Amendment right to avoid answering questions. This constitutional right allows a person to refuse to provide information that could be used against them in a criminal case. Senator Rand Paul led the questioning, focusing on the origins of the pandemic and past health policies. The event highlights the deep political divisions in the United States regarding the management of the health crisis.
summary.zh: 前美國頂尖衛生官員安東尼·佛奇近期出席美國參議院委員會。在聽證會期間，他選擇行使第五修正案權利以避免回答問題。這項憲法權利允許個人拒絕提供可能在刑事案件中對自己不利的資訊。藍德·保羅參議員主持了此次質詢，重點聚焦於疫情起源與過去的衛生政策。此事件凸顯了美國在處理這場健康危機上，存在著深刻的政治分歧。

paragraphs.en: Former top US health official Anthony Fauci recently appeared before a US Senate committee to discuss the origins of the Covid-19 pandemic. During the meeting, Dr. Fauci refused to answer questions from lawmakers more than 100 times. He explained that he was following the advice of his lawyers to protect himself from potential legal trouble.
paragraphs.zh: 前美國頂尖衛生官員安東尼·佛奇（Anthony Fauci）近期出席美國參議院委員會，討論新冠肺炎疫情的起源。在會議期間，佛奇博士拒絕回答議員提問超過一百次。他解釋說，這是遵循律師的建議，以保護自己免於潛在的法律糾紛。

paragraphs.en: Dr. Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment to the US Constitution. This is a legal right that says a person cannot be forced to act as a witness against themselves in a criminal case. According to BBC News, Dr. Fauci stated that he feared Republican lawmakers would try to use his words to prosecute him for perjury, which is the crime of lying while under oath. He noted that he has already testified at several other hearings about the pandemic and its origins.
paragraphs.zh: 佛奇博士援引了美國憲法第五修正案。這是一項法律權利，規定個人在刑事案件中不得被強迫擔任不利於自己的證人。根據英國廣播公司新聞網（BBC News）報導，佛奇博士表示，他擔心共和黨籍議員會試圖利用他的言論來控告他犯下偽證罪，也就是在宣誓後說謊的罪行。他指出，自己先前已針對疫情及其起源在其他多場聽證會上作證。

paragraphs.en: At 85 years old, Dr. Fauci is the former leader of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID). During the hearing, he told the Senate Committee on Homeland Security that he felt Senator Rand Paul, who led the meeting, had an "obvious obsession" with him. Dr. Fauci suggested that the senator’s main goal was to find a way to put him "behind bars." He stated that he had great respect for the government, but he felt he had no choice but to remain silent to avoid being trapped by the questioning.
paragraphs.zh: 現年八十五歲的佛奇博士是美國國家過敏與傳染病研究院（NIAID）的前任院長。在聽證會上，他向參議院國土安全委員會表示，他認為主持會議的藍德·保羅（Rand Paul）參議員對他有「明顯的執念」。佛奇博士暗示，該位參議員的主要目標是想方設法將他「關進大牢」。他表示自己對政府懷有崇高的敬意，但為了避免落入質詢的陷阱，他認為自己別無選擇，只能保持沉默。

paragraphs.en: Senator Rand Paul, who was an eye surgeon before entering politics, continued to ask questions even after Dr. Fauci refused to speak. The senator repeatedly asked Dr. Fauci to apologize for his past actions. According to BBC News, Senator Paul said the committee would vote next week on a resolution to hold Dr. Fauci in contempt of Congress, which is a formal way of saying someone has disobeyed or disrespected the legislative body.
paragraphs.zh: 曾任眼科醫師、後轉入政壇的藍德·保羅參議員，即便在佛奇博士拒絕發言後仍持續提問。該位參議員多次要求佛奇博士為其過去的行為道歉。根據英國廣播公司新聞網報導，保羅參議員表示，委員會將於下週投票表決一項決議，以認定佛奇博士藐視國會，這是一種正式指控某人違抗或不尊重立法機關的說法。

paragraphs.en: Republicans have long accused Dr. Fauci of hiding information about the pandemic and lying about the dangers of the virus. In the past, Dr. Fauci has denied these claims, calling them "simply preposterous." During the hearing, the discussion also covered shifting health guidance. These are the rules and advice from officials that changed during the pandemic as scientists learned more about the disease. Dr. Fauci has previously defended his policy decisions, noting that health officials were learning in real-time.
paragraphs.zh: 共和黨人長期以來指控佛奇博士隱瞞疫情資訊，並在病毒危險性上撒謊。過去，佛奇博士曾否認這些指控，稱其「簡直荒謬」。在聽證會期間，討論內容也涵蓋了不斷變動的衛生指引。這些指引是指官員在疫情期間，隨著科學家對疾病了解加深而隨之調整的規則與建議。佛奇博士先前曾為自己的政策決定辯護，指出衛生官員是在即時學習的過程中做出決策。

paragraphs.en: The situation became even more tense when one of Dr. Fauci’s lawyers, David Schertler, was removed from the room. Mr. Schertler had tried to speak up during the questioning to make a legal point. Later, he called the removal "outrageous" and described the hearing as a personal attack against his client. He claimed the event showed a "vindictive nature" from those leading the investigation.
paragraphs.zh: 當佛奇博士的律師之一大衛·謝特勒（David Schertler）被請出會議室時，情況變得更加緊張。謝特勒先生在質詢過程中試圖發言以提出法律觀點。事後，他稱此舉「令人憤慨」，並形容這場聽證會是對他當事人的人身攻擊。他聲稱此事件顯示了調查主導者具有「報復心態」。

paragraphs.en: This hearing is part of a larger, ongoing debate in the United States about how the pandemic began. The origins of the virus have been a subject of intense argument for years. Former President Donald Trump, who was in office when the pandemic began, used social media to criticize Dr. Fauci during the hearing. Mr. Trump repeated his belief that the virus came from a laboratory in Wuhan, China, and accused Dr. Fauci of trying to protect China during his time in office.
paragraphs.zh: 這場聽證會是美國國內關於疫情起源長期爭論的一部分。病毒的起源多年來一直是激烈辯論的主題。在疫情爆發時擔任總統的前總統唐納·川普（Donald Trump），在聽證會期間透過社群媒體批評佛奇博士。川普先生重申他認為病毒來自中國武漢實驗室的觀點，並指控佛奇博士在任職期間試圖袒護中國。

paragraphs.en: It is important to understand that using the Fifth Amendment is not an admission of guilt. It is a legal tool designed to protect people from unfair pressure or mistakes. While former President Joe Biden gave Dr. Fauci a pre-emptive pardon—an official act that forgives someone for past crimes—this protection only covers actions taken between 2014 and 2025. Dr. Fauci could still face legal issues for actions taken after that date, or from state and local authorities.
paragraphs.zh: 必須了解的是，行使第五修正案並不等同於認罪。這是一項旨在保護民眾免受不公平壓力或錯誤指控的法律工具。雖然前總統喬·拜登（Joe Biden）給予佛奇博士預防性特赦——這是一項免除某人過去罪行的正式行政行為——但此保護僅涵蓋二零一四年至二零二五年期間的行為。佛奇博士仍可能因該日期之後的行為，或面臨州與地方當局的法律問題。

paragraphs.en: As the situation continues, the divide between health officials and certain political leaders remains clear. For many, this hearing represents the deep frustration and disagreement that has defined the American response to the health crisis. Whether this leads to further legal action or simply remains a political standoff is something that will likely be decided in the coming weeks.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著事態發展，衛生官員與特定政治領袖之間的分歧依然明顯。對許多人而言，這場聽證會代表了美國在應對這場健康危機時所面臨的深刻挫折與分歧。這是否會導致進一步的法律行動，抑或僅維持政治僵局，很可能在未來幾週內見分曉。

keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個常見的隱喻用法，字面上是「在柵欄後面」，實際指入獄。文中：Dr. Fauci suggested that the senator’s main goal was to find a way to put him "behind bars."

keyTerms.definitionEn: To express one's opinion or interrupt a conversation to make a point.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 發言、大聲說出意見、插話。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指在正式場合中為了表達法律觀點而發言。文中：Mr. Schertler had tried to speak up during the questioning to make a legal point.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A situation in which neither side in a fight or argument can make any progress.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常用於描述政治或談判中雙方互不相讓的狀態。文中：Whether this leads to further legal action or simply remains a political standoff is something that will likely be decided in the coming weeks.

quiz.question: According to the article, why did Dr. Fauci choose to remain silent during the Senate hearing?

options.A: He wanted to protest the removal of his lawyer from the room.
options.B: He was following legal advice to avoid potential accusations of perjury.
options.C: He believed the committee members were not qualified to ask about the pandemic.
options.D: He was instructed by former President Joe Biden to avoid speaking to lawmakers.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 B。文章第二段明確提到，Dr. Fauci 援引美國憲法第五修正案，是為了聽從律師建議，以避免被共和黨議員指控偽證罪（perjury）。選項 A 的律師被趕出場是後來發生的事，並非他保持沈默的最初原因。選項 C 文章未提及。選項 D 雖然提到總統給予特赦，但並未指示他保持沈默。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between Dr. Fauci and Senator Rand Paul?

options.A: They have a long history of professional collaboration in medical research.
options.B: They share similar views on how the pandemic should have been managed.
options.C: There is a significant level of personal and political animosity between them.
options.D: They are working together to uncover the true origins of the virus.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 C。從第三段 Dr. Fauci 提到參議員 Rand Paul 對他有「明顯的執念」（obvious obsession），且意圖將他「關進監獄」，以及第四段提到參議員持續逼問並試圖以藐視國會罪名對付他，可以推論雙方存在嚴重的敵對與政治對立關係。選項 A、B、D 皆與文章描述的緊張對立情勢完全不符。

quiz.question: In the sixth paragraph, what does the word 'vindictive' most likely mean?

options.A: Seeking revenge or desiring to cause harm to someone.
options.B: Highly organized and professional in conduct.
options.D: Extremely tired after a long period of work.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 A。文中提到律師認為聽證會是一場「個人攻擊」，並形容領導調查的人具有「vindictive nature」，結合前後文對聽證會充滿敵意與攻擊性的描述，vindictive 指的是「報復性的」或「懷恨在心的」。選項 B、C、D 皆與此處表達的負面指控語氣不符。

quiz.question: What is the primary focus of this article?

options.A: A detailed scientific explanation of how the Covid-19 virus originated.
options.B: The legal history and importance of the Fifth Amendment in the US.
options.C: The personal life and medical career of Dr. Anthony Fauci.
options.D: The contentious political conflict surrounding Dr. Fauci’s testimony on the pandemic.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 D。本文的核心在於描述 Dr. Fauci 在國會聽證會上拒絕回答問題的政治僵局，以及這場聽證會如何反映美國對疫情應對的深刻分歧與政治對立。選項 A 僅是背景議題而非本文焦點；選項 B 僅是解釋為何 Fauci 能沈默的工具；選項 C 雖涉及 Fauci，但重點在於他在聽證會上的遭遇與爭議，而非他的職業生涯全貌。
